# New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod

## SYNOPSIS

Builds a maintenance time period for the -TimePeriod of New-ZbxMaintenance and Set-ZbxMaintenance.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod [[-TimePeriodType] <ZabbixTimePeriodType>] [-Period <string>] [-StartDate <DateTimeOffset>] [-StartTime <TimeOnly>] [-Every <int>] [-Day <int>] [-DayOfWeek <int>] [-Month <int>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A time period says when a maintenance is in effect: once, or every day, week or month at a time of day. The New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod cmdlet writes it as a hashtable keyed by the API's field names, which the -TimePeriod of New-ZbxMaintenance and Set-ZbxMaintenance take as it is, alone or in an array. -TimePeriodType is positional. Nothing is sent to the server, so the command needs no connection.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Build a one-time window and use it in a maintenance

```powershell
$start = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.AddHours(1).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$window = New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Onetime -StartDate $start -Period 7200
New-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Patch window' -Host 'web-01' -ActiveSince $start -ActiveTill ($start + 7200) -TimePeriod $window |
    Select-Object MaintenanceId, Name
```

A Onetime period starts at -StartDate (Unix seconds) and lasts -Period seconds. The builder only writes a hashtable in the wire shape; New-ZbxMaintenance sends it in -TimePeriod.

### Example 2: A weekly window: Sundays 02:00 to 04:00

```powershell
$weekly = New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Weekly -Every 1 -DayOfWeek 64 -StartTime '02:00' -Period (2 * 3600)
$since = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$null = New-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Sunday patching' -Group 'Web servers' -ActiveSince $since -ActiveTill ($since + 90 * 86400) -TimePeriod $weekly
(Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Sunday patching' -SelectTimePeriods).TimePeriods | Format-Table timeperiod_type, every, dayofweek, start_time, period
```

Weekly periods use -DayOfWeek as a bit mask (Monday = 1 ... Sunday = 64), -StartTime as the time of day and -Every as the week interval. -SelectTimePeriods reads the stored periods back.

### Example 3: Several windows in one maintenance: the last Friday of every month, and every night

```powershell
$periods = @(
    New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Monthly -Every 5 -DayOfWeek 16 -Month 4095 -StartTime '22:00' -Period 3600
    New-ZbxMaintenanceTimePeriod -TimePeriodType Daily -Every 1 -StartTime '03:00' -Period 900
)
$since = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$null = New-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Month-end freeze' -Host 'db-01' -ActiveSince $since -ActiveTill ($since + 365 * 86400) -TimePeriod $periods
(Get-ZbxMaintenance -Name 'Month-end freeze' -SelectTimePeriods).TimePeriods | Format-Table timeperiod_type, every, dayofweek, month, start_time, period
```

A Monthly period with -Every 5 (the API's "last" week) and -DayOfWeek 16 (Friday) means "the last Friday"; -Month is a bit mask of months (4095 = all twelve). -TimePeriod takes an array, so one maintenance can hold several windows.

## PARAMETERS

### -Period

Duration of the maintenance window, in seconds or as a time suffix, from 5 minutes to just under 1000 days; the default is 1 hour.
